name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CLASS12_HUMAN_REPRODUCTION_STMTMULTI_Q02 - Female reproductive tract histology fimbriae and pubertal follicle reserve

questiontext.text:
Given below are five statements regarding the female reproductive system and ovarian follicular dynamics:

Statement I: The oviduct consists of the infundibulum, the ampulla, and the narrow-lumened isthmus.

Statement II: Fimbriae are finger-like projections at the margins of the infundibulum that collect the ovum after ovulation.

Statement III: The cervix and vagina together constitute the birth canal.

Statement IV: At puberty, each human ovary contains approximately 2 million fully mature Graafian follicles.

Statement V: The clitoris is a tiny finger-like structure that lies at the upper junction of the two labia minora above the urethral opening.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

मादा जनन तंत्र और डिम्बग्रंथि कूपिक गतिशीलता के संदर्भ में नीचे पाँच कथन दिए गए हैं:

कथन I: अंडवाहिनी में कीपक (इन्फंडीबुलम), तुम्बिका (एम्पुला) और संकीर्ण गुहा वाला इस्थमस शामिल होते हैं।

कथन II: झालर (फिम्ब्री) कीपक के किनारों पर अंगुली सदृश प्रवर्ध हैं जो अंडोत्सर्ग के बाद अंडाणु को एकत्रित करते हैं।

कथन III: ग्रीवा (सर्विक्स) और योनि मिलकर प्रसव मार्ग (बर्थ कैनाल) बनाते हैं।

कथन IV: यौवनारंभ के समय प्रत्येक मानव अंडाशय में लगभग 20 लाख पूर्ण परिपक्व ग्राफी कूपक होते हैं।

कथन V: भगशेफ (क्लिटोरिस) एक सूक्ष्म अंगुली जैसी संरचना है जो मूत्र द्वार के ऊपर दोनों लघु भगोष्ठों के ऊपरी जोड़ पर स्थित होती है।

उपर्युक्त कथनों के आलोक में, नीचे दिए गए विकल्पों में से सही उत्तर का चयन कीजिए:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of oviduct structural subdivisions
The fallopian tube extends approximately 10 to 12 cm from the ovary to the uterus, sequentially consisting of the funnel-like infundibulum, the wide ampulla, and the narrow isthmus. Hence, this anatomical premise is accurate.

Step 2: Evaluation of fimbriae morphology and ovum pick-up
Ciliated finger-like fimbriae fringe the abdominal ostium of the infundibulum and rhythmically sweep across the ovarian surface during ovulation to capture the extruded secondary oocyte. Thus, this functional description is correct.

Step 3: Evaluation of the birth canal components
Anatomically and obstetrically, the cervical canal of the uterine cervix in continuity with the distensible vaginal lumen forms the functional birth canal through which the fetus passes during parturition. Therefore, this statement is factually true.

Step 4: Evaluation of pubertal ovarian follicular reserve
Due to extensive follicular atresia throughout childhood, only 60,000 to 80,000 primary follicles remain in each ovary at puberty, not 2 million Graafian follicles. Mature Graafian follicles develop cyclically one per cycle after puberty, never in millions. Hence, this quantitative claim is vastly incorrect.

Step 5: Evaluation of clitoral anatomical coordinates
The clitoris is an erectile homologous organ situated at the anterior convergence of the bilateral labia minora cranial to the external urethral orifice. Thus, this topographical location is valid.

Step 6: Interdependence and synthesis
The structural subdivisions of the oviduct, the capture function of fimbriae, the composition of the birth canal, and clitoral coordinates are accurate, whereas the quantitative follicle count at puberty is biologically erroneous.

Conclusion: The assertions regarding oviduct anatomy, fimbriae function, the birth canal, and clitoral location are correct, whereas the assertion regarding pubertal follicle numbers is incorrect.

चरण 1: अंडवाहिनी के भागों का मूल्यांकन
अंडवाहिनी कीपक, तुम्बिका और संकीर्ण पथ (इस्थमस) से मिलकर बनी होती है। अतः यह संरचनात्मक विवरण सही है।

चरण 2: झालर (फिम्ब्री) के कार्य का मूल्यांकन
कीपक के किनारों पर स्थित अंगुली सदृश झालर अंडोत्सर्ग के बाद अंडाणु को एकत्रित करते हैं। अतः यह कथन सही है।

चरण 3: प्रसव मार्ग (बर्थ कैनाल) के घटकों का मूल्यांकन
ग्रीवा गुहा और योनि मिलकर प्रसव मार्ग बनाते हैं जिससे होकर शिशु का जन्म होता है। अतः यह विवरण सत्य है।

चरण 4: यौवनारंभ पर कूपिक संख्या का मूल्यांकन
यौवनारंभ के समय प्रत्येक अंडाशय में केवल 60,000 से 80,000 प्राथमिक कूपक ही बचते हैं, न कि 20 लाख ग्राफी कूपक। ग्राफी कूपक तो चक्र में एक-एक करके परिपक्व होते हैं। अतः यह कथन गलत है।

चरण 5: भगशेफ (क्लिटोरिस) की स्थिति का मूल्यांकन
भगशेफ मूत्र द्वार के ऊपर दोनों लघु भगोष्ठों के ऊपरी जोड़ पर स्थित एक सूक्ष्म अंगुली सदृश संरचना है। अतः यह कथन सही है।

चरण 6: परस्पर निर्भरता और निष्कर्ष
अंडवाहिनी के भाग, झालर का कार्य, प्रसव मार्ग और भगशेफ की स्थिति सही हैं, जबकि यौवन पर कूपकों की संख्या वाला कथन गलत है।

निष्कर्ष: अंडवाहिनी की संरचना, झालर के कार्य, प्रसव मार्ग और भगशेफ की स्थिति से संबंधित कथन सही हैं, जबकि यौवन पर कूपकों की संख्या से संबंधित कथन गलत है।

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CLASS12_HUMAN_REPRODUCTION_STMTMULTI_Q03 - Sperm head acrosome mitochondrial middle piece and semen parameters

questiontext.text:
Given below are five statements regarding sperm ultrastructure, seminal plasma, and semen parameters:

Statement I: The sperm head contains an elongated haploid nucleus covered anteriorly by a cap-like acrosome.

Statement II: The middle piece of the sperm possesses numerous mitochondria that produce energy for flagellar movement.

Statement III: Seminal plasma is rich in fructose, calcium, and certain enzymes.

Statement IV: The human male ejaculates about 200 to 300 million sperms during a single coitus.

Statement V: For normal fertility, at least 99 percent of sperms must exhibit complete immobility.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

शुक्राणु की सूक्ष्म संरचना, वीर्य प्लाज्मा और वीर्य मापदंडों के संदर्भ में नीचे पाँच कथन दिए गए हैं:

कथन I: शुक्राणु के शीर्ष में एक दीर्घीकृत अगुणित केंद्रक होता है जो अग्र भाग में टोपी जैसी संरचना (एक्रोसोम) से ढका होता है।

कथन II: शुक्राणु के मध्य खंड में अनेक माइटोकॉन्ड्रिया होते हैं जो कशाभी गति के लिए ऊर्जा उत्पन्न करते हैं।

कथन III: वीर्य प्लाज्मा फ्रुक्टोज, कैल्शियम और कुछ एंजाइमों से भरपूर होता है।

कथन IV: मानव नर एक मैथुन के दौरान लगभग 200 से 300 मिलियन शुक्राणु स्खलित करता है।

कथन V: सामान्य उर्वरता के लिए, कम से कम 99 प्रतिशत शुक्राणुओं में पूर्ण गतिहीनता होनी चाहिए।

उपर्युक्त कथनों के आलोक में, नीचे दिए गए विकल्पों में से सही उत्तर का चयन कीजिए:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of sperm head architecture
The apical region of a spermatozoon features a compact, condensed haploid nucleus hooded by the acrosomal vesicle containing hyaluronidase and acrosin enzymes. Thus, this structural statement is accurate.

Step 2: Evaluation of middle piece energetics
The cylindrical middle piece encloses a dense spiral sheath of mitochondria that perform oxidative phosphorylation to synthesize ATP for the axial axoneme tail. Hence, this physiological role is correct.

Step 3: Evaluation of seminal plasma biochemical composition
Secretions from seminal vesicles, prostate, and bulbourethral glands pool to form seminal plasma rich in fructose (nutrient substrate), calcium ions, and clotting/fibrinolytic enzymes. Therefore, this biochemical summary is factual.

Step 4: Evaluation of typical ejaculate sperm count
Clinical and physiological measurements confirm that an adult male discharges an average volume of semen containing approximately 200 to 300 million spermatozoa per ejaculation. Thus, this numerical estimate is correct.

Step 5: Evaluation of sperm motility requirements for fertility
Normal reproductive fertility mandates that at least 60% of ejaculated spermatozoa possess normal morphology and at least 40% show vigorous forward progressive motility. Requiring 99% immobility represents severe asthenozoospermia causing absolute infertility. Therefore, this assertion is completely false.

Step 6: Interdependence and synthesis
The anatomical features of the sperm head and middle piece, the composition of seminal plasma, and the standard ejaculate count are biologically correct, whereas claiming normal fertility requires 99% immobility is absurdly incorrect.

Conclusion: The assertions regarding sperm head morphology, middle piece mitochondria, seminal plasma constituents, and ejaculate count are correct, whereas the assertion regarding sperm immobility is incorrect.

चरण 1: शुक्राणु शीर्ष की संरचना का मूल्यांकन
शुक्राणु के शीर्ष में अगुणित केंद्रक होता है जो अग्र भाग में एक्रोसोम (टोपी जैसी संरचना) से ढका होता है। अतः यह विवरण सही है।

चरण 2: मध्य खंड के माइटोकॉन्ड्रिया का मूल्यांकन
मध्य खंड में अनेक माइटोकॉन्ड्रिया होते हैं जो पूंछ की गतिशीलता के लिए आवश्यक ऊर्जा प्रदान करते हैं। अतः यह कथन सही है।

चरण 3: वीर्य प्लाज्मा के रासायनिक संघटन का मूल्यांकन
सहायक ग्रंथियों का स्राव (वीर्य प्लाज्मा) फ्रुक्टोज, कैल्शियम और विशिष्ट एंजाइमों से समृद्ध होता है। अतः यह विवरण सही है।

चरण 4: स्खलन में शुक्राणुओं की कुल संख्या का मूल्यांकन
एक सामान्य मैथुन के दौरान लगभग 200 से 300 मिलियन शुक्राणु स्खलित होते हैं। अतः यह संख्यात्मक मान सत्य है।

चरण 5: सामान्य उर्वरता हेतु गतिशीलता के मानक का मूल्यांकन
सामान्य उर्वरता के लिए कम से कम 60% सामान्य आकार के और कम से कम 40% तीव्र गतिशील होने चाहिए। 99% शुक्राणुओं को गतिहीन बताना बंध्यता का कारण है, उर्वरता का नहीं। अतः यह कथन गलत है।

चरण 6: परस्पर निर्भरता और निष्कर्ष
शुक्राणु शीर्ष, मध्य खंड, वीर्य प्लाज्मा और कुल संख्या से संबंधित विवरण सत्य हैं, जबकि 99% गतिहीनता की आवश्यकता वाला दावा गलत है।

निष्कर्ष: शुक्राणु शीर्ष, मध्य खंड के माइटोकॉन्ड्रिया, वीर्य प्लाज्मा के घटकों और स्खलन में शुक्राणुओं की संख्या से संबंधित कथन सही हैं, जबकि शुक्राणुओं की गतिहीनता से संबंधित कथन गलत है।

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CLASS12_HUMAN_REPRODUCTION_STMTMULTI_Q04 - Menstrual cycle gonadotropin peaks ovulation and corpus luteum steroidogenesis

questiontext.text:
Given below are five statements regarding the endocrine regulation of the primate menstrual cycle:

Statement I: Menstruation occurs only when the released ovum is not fertilised.

Statement II: Secretion of LH and FSH increases gradually during the follicular phase, stimulating follicular development and estrogen secretion.

Statement III: A sharp mid-cycle LH surge induces rupture of the mature Graafian follicle and releases the secondary oocyte.

Statement IV: The corpus luteum secretes large amounts of progesterone essential for maintaining the endometrium.

Statement V: During pregnancy, cyclic menstruation continues uninterrupted every month without any hormonal cessation.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

प्राइमेट मासिक धर्म चक्र का अंतःस्रावी नियमन के संदर्भ में नीचे पाँच कथन दिए गए हैं:

कथन I: मासिक स्राव केवल तभी होता है जब मुक्त हुआ अंडाणु निषेचित नहीं होता है।

कथन II: कूपिक प्रावस्था के दौरान LH और FSH का स्राव धीरे-धीरे बढ़ता है, जो कूपिक विकास और एस्ट्रोजेन स्राव को उत्तेजित करता है।

कथन III: मध्य-चक्र में LH की तीव्र वृद्धि (LH सर्ज) परिपक्व ग्राफी कूपक को फाड़कर द्वितीयक अंडक को मुक्त करती है।

कथन IV: पीत पिंड (कॉर्पस ल्यूटियम) एंडोमेट्रियम को बनाए रखने के लिए आवश्यक भारी मात्रा में प्रोजेस्टेरोन स्रावित करता है।

कथन V: गर्भावस्था के दौरान, बिना किसी हार्मोनल रुकावट के हर महीने चक्रीय मासिक धर्म निर्बाध रूप से जारी रहता है।

उपर्युक्त कथनों के आलोक में, नीचे दिए गए विकल्पों में से सही उत्तर का चयन कीजिए:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of the prerequisite for menstrual shedding
In an infertile cycle, the corpus luteum involutes, withdrawing progesterone and triggering the ischemic necrosis and sloughing of the functional endometrium. If fertilisation occurs, embryonic hCG sustains progesterone, preventing menstruation. Hence, this physiological statement is correct.

Step 2: Evaluation of follicular gonadotropin elevation
During the pre-ovulatory proliferative phase, rising anterior pituitary gonadotropins (FSH and LH) drive antral development in the cohort of ovarian follicles, promoting granulosa cell proliferation and estradiol production. Thus, this endocrine progression is accurate.

Step 3: Evaluation of the ovulatory LH surge
Positive feedback from high threshold estrogen triggers a massive surge of pituitary LH around day 14, stimulating collagenases and prostaglandins that rupture the dominant Graafian follicle and discharge the oocyte. Hence, this ovulatory trigger is correct.

Step 4: Evaluation of corpus luteum progestational activity
Post-ovulatory luteinization of the collapsed follicle yields the corpus luteum, whose specialized cells synthesize high levels of progesterone to maintain glandular tortuosity and vascularity in the endometrium for blastocyst implantation. Therefore, this luteal role is valid.

Step 5: Evaluation of menstruation during pregnancy
During gestation, persistent placental and luteal progesterone and estrogens impose potent negative feedback on the hypothalamic-pituitary axis, arresting follicular recruitment and causing complete amenorrhea. Claiming that menstruation continues uninterrupted during pregnancy directly contradicts human reproductive endocrinology.

Step 6: Interdependence and synthesis
The causal factors of menses, gonadotropin dynamics in the follicular phase, LH-triggered ovulation, and corpus luteum progesterone secretion are validated facts, whereas asserting that menstruation occurs during pregnancy is false.

Conclusion: The assertions regarding fertilisation absence causing menses, follicular gonadotropins, mid-cycle LH surge, and corpus luteum function are correct, whereas the assertion claiming menstruation continues during pregnancy is incorrect.

चरण 1: मासिक स्राव की शर्त का मूल्यांकन
मासिक धर्म केवल तभी होता है जब मुक्त हुआ अंडाणु निषेचित नहीं होता, क्योंकि निषेचन न होने पर ही प्रोजेस्टेरोन का स्तर गिरता है। अतः यह कथन सही है।

चरण 2: कूपिक प्रावस्था में गोनाडोट्रोपिन के स्राव का मूल्यांकन
कूपिक प्रावस्था में LH और FSH धीरे-धीरे बढ़ते हैं जिससे कूपक विकसित होते हैं और एस्ट्रोजेन का स्राव बढ़ता है। अतः यह अंतःस्रावी चरण सत्य है।

चरण 3: मध्य-चक्र LH सर्ज और अंडोत्सर्ग का मूल्यांकन
चक्र के मध्य में होने वाला तीव्र LH सर्ज परिपक्व ग्राफी कूपक को फाड़कर अंडोत्सर्ग (अंडाणु की मुक्ति) कराता है। अतः यह विवरण सही है।

चरण 4: कॉर्पस ल्यूटियम द्वारा प्रोजेस्टेरोन स्राव का मूल्यांकन
अंडोत्सर्ग के बाद बना कॉर्पस ल्यूटियम भारी मात्रा में प्रोजेस्टेरोन बनाता है जो एंडोमेट्रियम को बनाए रखने के लिए आवश्यक है। अतः यह कथन सत्य है।

चरण 5: गर्भावस्था के दौरान मासिक धर्म का मूल्यांकन
गर्भावस्था के दौरान मासिक चक्र की सभी घटनाएं रुक जाती हैं और कोई मासिक धर्म नहीं होता। गर्भावस्था में निर्बाध मासिक धर्म का दावा पूरी तरह गलत है।

चरण 6: परस्पर निर्भरता और निष्कर्ष
मासिक स्राव का कारण, कूपिक प्रावस्था, LH सर्ज और प्रोजेस्टेरोन स्राव सही हैं, जबकि गर्भावस्था में मासिक धर्म जारी रहने वाला कथन गलत है।

निष्कर्ष: निषेचन न होने पर मासिक स्राव, कूपिक गोनाडोट्रोपिन, मध्य-चक्र LH सर्ज और कॉर्पस ल्यूटियम के कार्य से संबंधित कथन सही हैं, जबकि गर्भावस्था में मासिक स्राव जारी रहने का दावा गलत है।

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CLASS12_HUMAN_REPRODUCTION_STMTMULTI_Q05 - Fertilisation cleavage blastomeres morula and blastocyst implantation

questiontext.text:
Given below are five statements regarding fertilisation, cleavage division, morula, blastocyst formation, and implantation:

Statement I: The sperm acrosome releases hydrolytic enzymes that digest through the corona radiata and zona pellucida to facilitate gamete fusion.

Statement II: Contact with the zona pellucida induces membrane alterations that permanently block the entry of polyspermic sperms.

Statement III: The solid ball of 8 to 16 blastomeres formed by early cleavage divisions is termed a morula.

Statement IV: In the blastocyst, the outer trophoblast layer attaches to the endometrium, while the inner cell mass differentiates into the embryo proper.

Statement V: Cleavage in human zygotes is characterized by massive cell growth that produces daughter blastomeres ten times larger than the original zygote.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

निषेचन, विदलन विभाजन, मोरुला, कोरकपुटी निर्माण और अंतरोपण के संदर्भ में नीचे पाँच कथन दिए गए हैं:

कथन I: शुक्राणु का एक्रोसोम जलअपघटनी एंजाइम छोड़ता है जो युग्मक संलयन को सुगम बनाने के लिए कोरोना रेडिएटा और जोना पेल्युसिडा को भेदते हैं।

कथन II: जोना पेल्युसिडा के साथ संपर्क झिल्ली में ऐसे परिवर्तन प्रेरित करता है जो अतिरिक्त शुक्राणुओं के प्रवेश को स्थायी रूप से रोकते हैं।

कथन III: प्रारंभिक विदलन विभाजनों द्वारा निर्मित 8 से 16 कोरकखंडों (ब्लास्टोमीयर्स) की ठोस गेंद को तूतक (मोरुला) कहा जाता है।

कथन IV: कोरकपुटी (ब्लास्टोसिस्ट) में, बाहरी पोषकोरक (ट्रोफोब्लास्ट) परत एंडोमेट्रियम से जुड़ती है, जबकि आंतरिक कोशिका समूह मुख्य भ्रूण के रूप में विभेदित होता है।

कथन V: मानव युग्मनज में विदलन की विशेषता भारी कोशिकीय वृद्धि है जो मूल युग्मनज से दस गुना बड़े संतति कोरकखंड उत्पन्न करती है।

उपर्युक्त कथनों के आलोक में, नीचे दिए गए विकल्पों में से सही उत्तर का चयन कीजिए:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of the acrosome reaction
The acrosomal cap undergoes exocytosis upon oocyte contact, discharging hyaluronidase and acrosin that disperse corona radiata granulosa cells and enzymatically digest a path through the glycoproteinaceous zona pellucida. Thus, this statement is factually accurate.

Step 2: Evaluation of the polyspermy block
Gamete fusion triggers the cortical reaction, modifying the zona pellucida architecture to establish a fast electrical and slow biochemical blockade against polyspermy. Hence, this monospermic protection mechanism is correctly stated.

Step 3: Evaluation of the morula stage
Mitotic cleavage through the 2-, 4-, and 8-cell stages yields a compact spherical cluster of 8 to 16 blastomeres resembling a mulberry, defined universally as the morula. Therefore, this developmental designation is correct.

Step 4: Evaluation of blastocyst tissue fates during implantation
Upon blastocoel cavitation, the blastocyst segregates into an outer trophoblast that invades maternal uterine endometrium and an inner cell mass (embryoblast) containing pluripotential stem cells that give rise to the three embryonic germ layers. Thus, these tissue fates are verified.

Step 5: Evaluation of cleavage blastomere size kinetics
Cleavage divisions represent rapid DNA replication and karyokinesis with truncated interphases lacking G1 and G2 cell growth phases. Consequently, blastomeres become progressively smaller at each successive cleavage division within the unchanged total volume bounded by the zona pellucida. Claiming that blastomeres grow ten times larger than the zygote is biological fantasy.

Step 6: Interdependence and synthesis
The mechanisms of acrosomal penetration, zona-mediated polyspermy block, morula structure, and blastocyst implantation are valid, whereas the assertion stating that cleavage increases blastomere size tenfold is completely false.

Conclusion: The assertions regarding acrosomal penetration, the polyspermy block, morula blastomeres, and blastocyst implantation are correct, whereas the assertion claiming tenfold blastomere growth during cleavage is incorrect.

चरण 1: एक्रोसोम अभिक्रिया का मूल्यांकन
एक्रोसोम से निकलने वाले एंजाइम कोरोना रेडिएटा और जोना पेल्युसिडा को भेदकर शुक्राणु के केंद्रक को अंडाणु में प्रवेश कराते हैं। अतः यह कथन सत्य है।

चरण 2: पॉलीस्पर्मी अवरोध का मूल्यांकन
शुक्राणु का जोना पेल्युसिडा से संपर्क झिल्ली में परिवर्तन लाकर अतिरिक्त शुक्राणुओं के प्रवेश को रोकता है (मोनोस्पर्मी सुनिश्चित करता है)। अतः यह विवरण सही है।

चरण 3: मोरुला (तूतक) अवस्था का मूल्यांकन
विदलन के दौरान 8 से 16 कोरकखंडों (ब्लास्टोमीयर्स) वाली ठोस भ्रूणीय गेंद को मोरुला कहा जाता है। अतः यह परिभाषा सही है।

चरण 4: अंतरोपण में ट्रोफोब्लास्ट और आंतरिक कोशिका समूह के कार्यों का मूल्यांकन
कोरकपुटी की बाहरी ट्रोफोब्लास्ट परत एंडोमेट्रियम से जुड़ती है और आंतरिक कोशिका समूह मुख्य भ्रूण के रूप में विकसित होता है। अतः यह कथन सही है।

चरण 5: विदलन में कोशिकाओं के आकार का मूल्यांकन
विदलन में कोशिका वृद्धि नहीं होती, जिससे प्रत्येक विभाजन के साथ कोशिकाएं छोटी होती जाती हैं। कोशिकाओं का मूल युग्मनज से दस गुना बड़ा होना बताना बिल्कुल गलत है।

चरण 6: परस्पर निर्भरता और निष्कर्ष
एक्रोसोम क्रिया, पॉलीस्पर्मी अवरोध, मोरुला निर्माण और अंतरोपण सही हैं, जबकि विदलन में कोशिकाओं का दस गुना बड़ा होना गलत है।

निष्कर्ष: एक्रोसोम वेधन, पॉलीस्पर्मी अवरोध, मोरुला कोरकखंड और कोरकपुटी अंतरोपण से संबंधित कथन सही हैं, जबकि विदलन में कोरकखंडों के दस गुना बड़े होने वाला कथन गलत है।

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CLASS12_HUMAN_REPRODUCTION_STMTMULTI_Q06 - Embryonic timeline fetal organogenesis neuroendocrine labor and colostrum

questiontext.text:
Given below are five statements regarding embryonic milestones, the neuroendocrine reflex of parturition, and lactation:

Statement I: In human beings, the embryo's heart is formed after one month of pregnancy.

Statement II: By the end of the second month of pregnancy, the foetus develops limbs and digits.

Statement III: The first movements of the foetus and appearance of hair on the head are usually observed during the fifth month.

Statement IV: The fetal ejection reflex triggers the release of oxytocin from the maternal posterior pituitary to cause stronger uterine contractions.

Statement V: Colostrum is toxic to the newborn baby and must be completely discarded by the mother.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

भ्रूणीय विकास के चरण, प्रसव का तंत्रिका-अंतःस्रावी प्रतिवर्त और स्तनपान के संदर्भ में नीचे पाँच कथन दिए गए हैं:

कथन I: मानव में गर्भावस्था के एक महीने बाद भ्रूण का हृदय बन जाता है।

कथन II: गर्भावस्था के दूसरे महीने के अंत तक भ्रूण में पाद (हाथ-पैर) और अंगुलियां विकसित हो जाती हैं।

कथन III: भ्रूण की पहली गति और सिर पर बालों का आना आमतौर पर पांचवें महीने के दौरान देखा जाता है।

कथन IV: भ्रूण निष्कासन प्रतिवर्त अधिक शक्तिशाली गर्भाशय संकुचन उत्पन्न करने के लिए मातृ पश्च पीयूष ग्रंथि से ऑक्सीटोसिन के स्राव को प्रेरित करता है।

कथन V: खीस (कोलोस्ट्रम) नवजात शिशु के लिए विषाक्त होता है और इसे मां द्वारा पूरी तरह से फेंक दिया जाना चाहिए।

उपर्युक्त कथनों के आलोक में, नीचे दिए गए विकल्पों में से सही उत्तर का चयन कीजिए:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of the one-month cardiac milestone
By approximately the fourth week of gestation (one month), the primitive heart tube establishes rhythmic pulsation, serving as the first detectable sign of life verifiable by auscultation with a sensitive stethoscope. Hence, this milestone is accurately stated.

Step 2: Evaluation of the two-month limb/digit milestone
By gestational week 8 (end of second month), the embryonic limb buds lengthen and separate to form distinct limbs and individual digits (fingers and toes). Thus, this developmental timeline is correct.

Step 3: Evaluation of the fifth-month movement and hair milestone
Quickening (maternal perception of fetal movements) and the development of fine scalp lanugo hair routinely occur during the fifth gestational month. Therefore, this chronological feature is factually sound.

Step 4: Evaluation of the neuroendocrine mechanism of parturition
Mechanical cervical stretching by the mature fetus and placenta induces the Ferguson reflex, transmitting afferent neural signals to the maternal hypothalamus to trigger oxytocin secretion from the neurohypophysis (posterior pituitary), which intensifies myometrial contractions via positive feedback. Thus, this mechanism is valid.

Step 5: Evaluation of colostrum immunological value
The initial postpartum mammary secretion, colostrum, is packed with proteins, growth factors, and maternal secretory antibodies (chiefly IgA) that confer vital passive mucosal immunity against infectious pathogens. Branding colostrum as toxic to be discarded is medically dangerous and directly contrary to established scientific doctrine.

Step 6: Interdependence and synthesis
The developmental milestones at month 1, month 2, and month 5, along with the oxytocin-mediated fetal ejection reflex, are medical facts, whereas designating colostrum as toxic is completely erroneous.

Conclusion: The assertions regarding embryonic heart formation, limb/digit development, fifth-month movements, and oxytocin-induced parturition are correct, whereas the assertion claiming colostrum is toxic is incorrect.

चरण 1: एक महीने पर हृदय निर्माण का मूल्यांकन
गर्भावस्था के एक महीने बाद भ्रूण का हृदय बन जाता है और धड़कने लगता है। अतः यह विकासात्मक चरण सही है।

चरण 2: दूसरे महीने के अंत में पाद और अंगुलियों के विकास का मूल्यांकन
दूसरे महीने के अंत तक भ्रूण में हाथ-पैर (पाद) और अंगुलियां विकसित हो जाती हैं। अतः यह कथन सत्य है।

चरण 3: पांचवें महीने में भ्रूण की गति और सिर के बालों का मूल्यांकन
गर्भावस्था के पांचवें महीने के दौरान भ्रूण की पहली गति महसूस होती है और सिर पर बाल दिखाई देने लगते हैं। अतः यह विवरण सही है।

चरण 4: प्रसव के न्यूरोएंडोक्राइन प्रतिवर्त का मूल्यांकन
भ्रूण निष्कासन प्रतिवर्त मातृ पश्च पीयूष ग्रंथि से ऑक्सीटोसिन के स्राव को प्रेरित करता है, जिससे गर्भाशय के संकुचन और अधिक तीव्र होते हैं। अतः यह तंत्र सही है।

चरण 5: खीस (कोलोस्ट्रम) के महत्व का मूल्यांकन
प्रसव के बाद शुरुआती दिनों का दूध (कोलोस्ट्रम) एंटीबॉडीज (विशेषकर IgA) से भरपूर होता है जो शिशु को बीमारियों से लड़ने की प्रतिरोधक क्षमता देता है। इसे विषाक्त और फेंकने योग्य बताना पूरी तरह गलत है।

चरण 6: परस्पर निर्भरता और निष्कर्ष
हृदय निर्माण, पाद/अंगुलियों का विकास, पांचवें महीने की गति और ऑक्सीटोसिन की भूमिका सही हैं, जबकि खीस को विषाक्त बताने वाला दावा गलत है।

निष्कर्ष: भ्रूणीय हृदय निर्माण, पाद व अंगुलियों के विकास, पांचवें महीने की गतिशीलता और ऑक्सीटोसिन द्वारा प्रसव से संबंधित कथन सही हैं, जबकि खीस (कोलोस्ट्रम) को विषाक्त बताने वाला कथन गलत है।

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_HUMAN_REPRODUCTION_MATCHING_Q01 - Matching male reproductive structures with functions

questiontext.text:
Match the male reproductive structures in List I with their corresponding descriptions or functions in List II:

List IList II
A. Leydig cellsI. Maintenance of low testicular temperature
B. Sertoli cellsII. Synthesis and secretion of androgens
C. ScrotumIII. Lubrication of the penis
D. Bulbourethral glandsIV. Providing nutrition to germ cells

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The male reproductive system consists of specialised structures, cells, and accessory glands that perform precise physiological roles in spermatogenesis, hormone production, and copulation.

Step 2: Evaluation of Pairs
Leydig cells (interstitial cells) are situated in the interstitial spaces outside the seminiferous tubules and synthesise and secrete testicular hormones termed androgens.
Sertoli cells line the inside of the seminiferous tubules and provide nutrition to the developing germ cells.
The scrotum is a pouch of skin hanging outside the abdominal cavity that keeps the testes at a temperature 2 to 2.5 degrees Celsius lower than normal internal body temperature, which is essential for spermatogenesis.
Bulbourethral glands (Cowper's glands) are paired accessory glands whose secretions assist in the lubrication of the penis.

Step 3: Pairing Summary and Final Conclusion
Matching each entry yields: Leydig cells with synthesis and secretion of androgens (A-II), Sertoli cells with providing nutrition to germ cells (B-IV), Scrotum with maintenance of low testicular temperature (C-I), and Bulbourethral glands with lubrication of the penis (D-III).
Final Answer: A-II, B-IV, C-I, D-III.

answer.text: A-II, B-IV, C-I, D-III
A-II, B-I, C-IV, D-III
A-IV, B-II, C-I, D-III
A-II, B-IV, C-III, D-I

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_HUMAN_REPRODUCTION_MATCHING_Q02 - Matching female external genitalia and duct structures

questiontext.text:

B. FimbriaeII. Cushion of fatty tissue covered by skin and pubic hair
C. ClitorisIII. Narrow canal forming birth canal with vagina

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The female reproductive anatomy incorporates accessory duct pathways and external genitalia, each characterised by distinctive anatomical features and specialized physiological roles.

Step 2: Evaluation of Pairs
Mons pubis is an external genital structure consisting of a cushion of fatty tissue covered by skin and pubic hair.
Fimbriae are finger-like projections at the margins of the infundibulum of the fallopian tube that facilitate collection of the ovulated secondary oocyte.
The clitoris is a tiny, sensitive finger-like erectile structure located at the anterior/upper junction of the two labia minora above the external urethral orifice.
The cervical canal is the cavity within the narrow cervix that unites with the vagina to form the birth canal.

Step 3: Pairing Summary and Final Conclusion
Combining these pairs gives: Mons pubis with cushion of fatty tissue covered by skin and pubic hair (A-II), Fimbriae with finger-like projections that help collect ovum (B-I), Clitoris with tiny finger-like structure at upper junction of labia minora (C-IV), and Cervical canal with narrow canal forming birth canal with vagina (D-III).
Final Answer: A-II, B-I, C-IV, D-III.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_HUMAN_REPRODUCTION_MATCHING_Q03 - Matching sperm structural components with functions

questiontext.text:
Match the parts of a human spermatozoon in List I with their respective functional or structural attributes in List II:

List IList II
A. AcrosomeI. Contains elongated haploid genetic material
B. HeadII. Envelope enclosing the entire body of sperm
C. Middle pieceIII. Cap-like structure filled with hydrolytic enzymes
D. Plasma membraneIV. Possesses numerous mitochondria producing energy for motility

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
A mature human spermatozoon is a microscopic flagellated gamete partitioned into four morphological zones: head, neck, middle piece, and tail, each possessing specialized organelles adapted for egg penetration and motility.

Step 2: Evaluation of Pairs
The acrosome is a cap-like structure covering the anterior portion of the sperm nucleus, rich in hydrolytic enzymes that digest egg envelopes to enable fertilisation.
The head contains an elongated haploid nucleus holding chromosomal material.
The middle piece contains numerous spirally arranged mitochondria that produce ATP as energy to power tail movements essential for motility.
A continuous plasma membrane envelops the entire outer body of the sperm cell.

Step 3: Pairing Summary and Final Conclusion
Correlating each structure gives: Acrosome with cap-like structure filled with hydrolytic enzymes (A-III), Head with contains elongated haploid genetic material (B-I), Middle piece with possesses numerous mitochondria producing energy for motility (C-IV), and Plasma membrane with envelope enclosing the entire body of sperm (D-II).
Final Answer: A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_HUMAN_REPRODUCTION_MATCHING_Q04 - Matching terms of male gamete differentiation and release

questiontext.text:
Match the physiological processes associated with reproduction in List I with their correct definitions in List II:

List IList II
A. SpermatogenesisI. Transformation of haploid spermatids into spermatozoa
B. SpermiogenesisII. Formation of sperms from immature male germ cells
C. SpermiationIII. Release of mature sperms from seminiferous tubules
D. InseminationIV. Transfer of sperms into the female genital tract

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The formation, morphological differentiation, release, and transfer of male gametes involve specific sequential steps governed by precise biological terminology.

Step 2: Evaluation of Pairs
Spermatogenesis is the complete developmental process wherein immature germ cells (spermatogonia) produce sperms in the seminiferous tubules.
Spermiogenesis refers specifically to the transformation of non-motile, circular haploid spermatids into flagellated spermatozoa.
Spermiation is the process by which mature sperm heads detach from Sertoli cells and are released into the lumen of the seminiferous tubules.
Insemination is the physical deposition and transfer of semen containing sperms into the female reproductive tract during coitus.

Step 3: Pairing Summary and Final Conclusion
Thus, the pairings are: Spermatogenesis with formation of sperms from immature male germ cells (A-II), Spermiogenesis with transformation of haploid spermatids into spermatozoa (B-I), Spermiation with release of mature sperms from seminiferous tubules (C-III), and Insemination with transfer of sperms into the female genital tract (D-IV).
Final Answer: A-II, B-I, C-III, D-IV.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_HUMAN_REPRODUCTION_MATCHING_Q05 - Matching ovarian follicular stages with histological features

questiontext.text:
Match the ovarian developmental stages in List I with their corresponding structural characteristics in List II:

List IList II
A. Primary follicleI. Appearance of fluid-filled cavity called antrum
B. Secondary follicleII. Degeneration into a progesterone-secreting endocrine body
C. Tertiary follicleIII. Primary oocyte surrounded by a single layer of granulosa cells
D. Corpus luteumIV. Primary oocyte surrounded by more granulosa layers and a new theca

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
During oogenesis and folliculogenesis, ovarian follicles transition through well-demarcated morphological phases accompanied by changes in cellular layers and antrum formation before ovulating and transforming into a temporary endocrine gland.

Step 2: Evaluation of Pairs
A primary follicle consists of a primary oocyte encapsulated by a single layer of granulosa cells.
A secondary follicle forms when the primary follicle acquires several additional layers of granulosa cells and a newly organised theca layer.
A tertiary follicle is distinguished by the development of a fluid-filled cavity called the antrum and the differentiation of the theca into theca interna and theca externa.
The corpus luteum is the yellowish endocrine structure formed from the ruptured remnants of the Graafian follicle following ovulation that synthesises abundant progesterone.

Step 3: Pairing Summary and Final Conclusion
The correct associations are: Primary follicle with primary oocyte surrounded by a single layer of granulosa cells (A-III), Secondary follicle with primary oocyte surrounded by more granulosa layers and a new theca (B-IV), Tertiary follicle with appearance of fluid-filled cavity called antrum (C-I), and Corpus luteum with degeneration into a progesterone-secreting endocrine body (D-II).
Final Answer: A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_HUMAN_REPRODUCTION_MATCHING_Q06 - Matching hormones of reproduction with target sites

questiontext.text:
Match the hormones in List I with their target action or primary source/function in List II:

List IList II
A. GnRHI. Acts on Sertoli cells to stimulate factors for spermiogenesis
B. LHII. Stimulates anterior pituitary to release gonadotropins
C. FSHIII. Stimulates Leydig cells to secrete androgens
D. ProgesteroneIV. Secreted by corpus luteum for maintenance of endometrium

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Reproductive physiology in both males and females is orchestrated by an endocrine cascade involving hypothalamic releasing hormones, anterior pituitary gonadotropins, and gonadal steroid hormones.

Step 2: Evaluation of Pairs
Gonadotropin-releasing hormone (GnRH) is a hypothalamic hormone that acts on the anterior pituitary to trigger synthesis and release of LH and FSH.
Luteinising hormone (LH) acts on testicular Leydig cells to stimulate the synthesis and secretion of androgens.
Follicle stimulating hormone (FSH) acts on Sertoli cells, inducing secretion of factors required for spermiogenesis.
Progesterone is produced in large quantities by the corpus luteum in the ovary and is essential for maintaining the glandular endometrium required for implantation.

Step 3: Pairing Summary and Final Conclusion
The correct alignment of hormones to their specific roles is: GnRH with stimulates anterior pituitary to release gonadotropins (A-II), LH with stimulates Leydig cells to secrete androgens (B-III), FSH with acts on Sertoli cells to stimulate factors for spermiogenesis (C-I), and Progesterone with secreted by corpus luteum for maintenance of endometrium (D-IV).
Final Answer: A-II, B-III, C-I, D-IV.

answer.text: A-II, B-III, C-I, D-IV
A-II, B-I, C-III, D-IV
A-III, B-II, C-I, D-IV
A-II, B-III, C-IV, D-I

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_HUMAN_REPRODUCTION_MATCHING_Q07 - Matching menstrual cycle phases with uterine ovarian events

questiontext.text:
Match the menstrual cycle phases in List I with their corresponding biological events in List II:

List IList II
A. Menstrual phaseI. Peak LH surge causing rupture of Graafian follicle
B. Follicular phaseII. Breakdown of endometrial lining accompanied by bleeding
C. Ovulatory phaseIII. Corpus luteum secretes progesterone to maintain endometrium
D. Luteal phaseIV. Follicle matures and endometrium regenerates through proliferation

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The primate menstrual cycle repeats at an average duration of 28 to 29 days, progressing through four continuous phases governed by dynamic feedback between pituitary gonadotropins and ovarian steroids.

Step 2: Evaluation of Pairs
During the menstrual phase (days 1-5), lack of progesterone causes disintegration of the vascularized uterine endometrium, causing menses.
During the follicular (proliferative) phase, developing follicles secrete estrogens which induce rapid repair and proliferation of the uterine endometrium.
The ovulatory phase around day 14 is triggered by a sudden mid-cycle peak in LH (LH surge), resulting in rupture of the mature Graafian follicle and release of the secondary oocyte.
The luteal (secretory) phase is marked by the presence of the corpus luteum, which secretes high amounts of progesterone necessary for preparing and maintaining the secretory endometrium.

Step 3: Pairing Summary and Final Conclusion
Assigning each phase to its characteristic event: Menstrual phase with breakdown of endometrial lining accompanied by bleeding (A-II), Follicular phase with follicle matures and endometrium regenerates through proliferation (B-IV), Ovulatory phase with peak LH surge causing rupture of Graafian follicle (C-I), and Luteal phase with corpus luteum secretes progesterone to maintain endometrium (D-III).
Final Answer: A-II, B-IV, C-I, D-III.

answer.text: A-II, B-IV, C-I, D-III
A-II, B-I, C-IV, D-III
A-IV, B-II, C-I, D-III
A-II, B-IV, C-III, D-I

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_HUMAN_REPRODUCTION_MATCHING_Q08 - Matching embryonic stages with structural cellular features

questiontext.text:
Match the embryonic stages or structures in List I with their descriptions in List II:

List IList II
A. BlastomeresI. Solid embryo possessing 8 to 16 cleavage cells
B. MorulaII. Outer layer that attaches directly to uterine endometrium
C. TrophoblastIII. Daughter cells formed through cleavage divisions of zygote
D. Inner cell massIV. Group of cells that differentiates into the embryo proper

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Following fertilisation in the ampullary-isthmic region, the zygote undergoes sequential cleavage divisions as it travels through the fallopian tube toward the uterine cavity, developing into discrete developmental stages.

Step 2: Evaluation of Pairs
Blastomeres are the individual diploid daughter cells generated by mitotic cleavage divisions of the single-celled zygote (producing 2, 4, 8, 16 cells).
A morula is a mulberry-shaped compact embryonic mass composed of 8 to 16 blastomeres.
The trophoblast is the outer epithelial shell of the blastocyst that establishes physical contact with and attaches to the maternal endometrium.
The inner cell mass is the centrally clustered group of cells within the blastocyst that later differentiates into the three germ layers of the developing embryo proper.

Step 3: Pairing Summary and Final Conclusion
Aligning each component produces: Blastomeres with daughter cells formed through cleavage divisions of zygote (A-III), Morula with solid embryo possessing 8 to 16 cleavage cells (B-I), Trophoblast with outer layer that attaches directly to uterine endometrium (C-II), and Inner cell mass with group of cells that differentiates into the embryo proper (D-IV).
Final Answer: A-III, B-I, C-II, D-IV.

answer.text: A-III, B-I, C-II, D-IV
A-III, B-II, C-I, D-IV
A-I, B-III, C-II, D-IV
A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_HUMAN_REPRODUCTION_MATCHING_Q09 - Matching human developmental milestones with gestational ages

questiontext.text:
Match the major developmental milestones of human foetal development in List I with their corresponding time of occurrence in List II:

List IList II
A. Heart is formedI. End of 12 weeks (first trimester)
B. Limbs and digits developII. After one month of pregnancy
C. Most major organ systems formedIII. By end of second month of pregnancy
D. Body covered with fine hair, eyelids separateIV. By end of 24 weeks (second trimester)

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Human embryonic and foetal development within the 9-month gestation period follows a well-defined chronological timeline of organogenesis and morphological changes.

Step 2: Evaluation of Pairs
After one month of pregnancy, the embryo's heart is formed and detectable via stethoscope.
By the end of the second month of pregnancy, the developing foetus forms distinct limbs and digits.
By the end of 12 weeks (first trimester), major organ systems are formed, including fully developed limbs and external genitalia.
By the end of 24 weeks (end of second trimester), the body is covered with fine hair, the eyelids separate, and eyelashes form.

Step 3: Pairing Summary and Final Conclusion
The correct match for each milestone is: Heart is formed with after one month of pregnancy (A-II), Limbs and digits develop with by end of second month of pregnancy (B-III), Most major organ systems formed with end of 12 weeks (first trimester) (C-I), and Body covered with fine hair, eyelids separate with by end of 24 weeks (second trimester) (D-IV).
Final Answer: A-II, B-III, C-I, D-IV.

answer.text: A-II, B-III, C-I, D-IV
A-III, B-II, C-I, D-IV
A-II, B-I, C-III, D-IV

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_HUMAN_REPRODUCTION_MATCHING_Q10 - Matching reproductive events with physiological regulatory mechanisms

questiontext.text:
Match the reproductive phenomena in List I with their underlying mechanisms or characteristics in List II:

List IList II
A. Cortical changes at zona pellucidaI. Mild uterine contractions induced by fully developed foetus and placenta
B. Foetal ejection reflexII. High antibody content providing passive immunity to new-born
C. Colostrum secretionIII. Block to polyspermy ensuring only one sperm fertilises the ovum
D. Acrosome reactionIV. Enzymatic penetration facilitating entry through ovum envelopes

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Events in fertilisation, parturition, and neonatal adaptation rely on precise cellular reactions and neuroendocrine reflexes designed to ensure successful reproduction and offspring survival.

Step 2: Evaluation of Pairs
When a fertilising sperm contacts the zona pellucida layer, it induces changes in the membrane that block the entry of additional sperms, thus preventing polyspermy.
The foetal ejection reflex originates from the mature foetus and placenta to generate mild uterine contractions that stimulate maternal pituitary oxytocin release.
Colostrum is the yellowish breast milk secreted during the initial days of lactation, rich in antibodies that confer critical resistance and passive immunity to the infant.
The acrosome reaction involves the release of acrosomal enzymes that digest the zona pellucida and corona radiata, facilitating sperm entry into the ooplasm.

Step 3: Pairing Summary and Final Conclusion
Pairing these physiological events gives: Cortical changes at zona pellucida with block to polyspermy ensuring only one sperm fertilises the ovum (A-III), Foetal ejection reflex with mild uterine contractions induced by fully developed foetus and placenta (B-I), Colostrum secretion with high antibody content providing passive immunity to new-born (C-II), and Acrosome reaction with enzymatic penetration facilitating entry through ovum envelopes (D-IV).
Final Answer: A-III, B-I, C-II, D-IV.

answer.text: A-III, B-I, C-II, D-IV
A-III, B-IV, C-II, D-I
A-I, B-III, C-II, D-IV
A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_HUMAN_REPRODUCTION_SEQUENCING_Q01 - Pathway of sperm transport in male accessory ducts

questiontext.text:
Arrange the following structures of the male reproductive system in the correct chronological order of sperm transport, starting from the site of production to the outside of the body:

  1. Epididymis
  2. Vasa efferentia
  3. Rete testis
  4. Seminiferous tubules
  5. Vas deferens
  6. Ejaculatory duct and urethra

Choose the correct sequence from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
In human males, sperms are produced in the testis and subsequently transported through a continuous series of intratesticular and extratesticular accessory ducts before exiting through the urethra.

Step 2: Sequential Evaluation of Pathway
First, spermatogenesis occurs within the highly coiled seminiferous tubules.
Second, the seminiferous tubules open into the rete testis, a network of tubular channels.
Third, the rete testis leads into fine ciliated ductules called the vasa efferentia that leave the testis.
Fourth, the vasa efferentia open into the epididymis along the posterior surface of the testis, where sperms undergo maturation and storage.
Fifth, the epididymis ascends as the vas deferens over the urinary bladder.
Sixth, the vas deferens receives a duct from the seminal vesicle to form the ejaculatory duct, which enters the urethra and terminates at the external urethral meatus.

Step 3: Verification of Sequence
Tracing the path step by step establishes the exact physiological order: Seminiferous tubules (IV) → Rete testis (III) → Vasa efferentia (II) → Epididymis (I) → Vas deferens (V) → Ejaculatory duct and urethra (VI).
Final Answer: IV → III → II → I → V → VI

answer.text: IV → II → III → I → V → VI
IV → III → II → I → V → VI
III → IV → II → I → V → VI
IV → III → I → II → V → VI

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_HUMAN_REPRODUCTION_SEQUENCING_Q02 - Sequence of events from fertilisation to implantation

questiontext.text:
Arrange the following reproductive and developmental events in the correct chronological sequence, starting from sperm-egg interaction to the establishment of pregnancy:

  1. Release of acrosomal enzymes inducing completion of meiosis II in the secondary oocyte
  2. Contact of sperm with the zona pellucida blocking additional sperm entry
  3. Attachment of the trophoblast to the uterine endometrium
  4. Fusion of the haploid male and female pronuclei to form a diploid zygote
  5. Transformation of morula into a blastocyst with inner cell mass and trophoblast
  6. Cleavage of zygote into 8 to 16 daughter cells called morula

Choose the correct sequence from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Human fertilisation and early embryogenesis proceed through an orderly succession of membrane reactions, meiotic completion, pronuclear fusion, mitotic cleavage, and blastocyst differentiation culminating in implantation.

Step 2: Sequential Evaluation of Developmental Events
First, a capacitated sperm binds to the zona pellucida of the secondary oocyte, triggering depolarisation and cortical reactions that block polyspermy.
Second, acrosomal secretions facilitate entry through the zona pellucida and oolemma, inducing the secondary oocyte to complete its arrested second meiotic division and produce a second polar body and ootid.
Third, the haploid nucleus of the sperm and that of the ovum fuse together during syngamy to form a single diploid zygote.
Fourth, the zygote undergoes rapid mitotic cleavage divisions as it travels through the isthmus toward the uterus, forming a solid sphere of 8 to 16 blastomeres termed the morula.
Fifth, continued mitotic division and fluid accumulation transform the morula into a hollow blastocyst comprising an outer trophoblast layer and an inner cell mass.
Sixth, the trophoblast layer adheres to the endometrium, and rapid division of uterine cells covers and embeds the blastocyst, completing implantation.

Step 3: Verification of Sequence
Ordering the events in chronological succession gives: Contact of sperm with zona pellucida (II) → Acrosomal entry and completion of meiosis II (I) → Fusion of pronuclei to form diploid zygote (IV) → Cleavage into morula (VI) → Transformation into blastocyst (V) → Attachment of trophoblast to endometrium (III).
Final Answer: II → I → IV → VI → V → III

answer.text: II → I → IV → V → VI → III
I → II → IV → VI → V → III
II → IV → I → VI → V → III
II → I → IV → VI → V → III

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_HUMANREPRODUCTION_MCQ_Q01 - Thermal regulation of testes in scrotum

questiontext.text: In human males, the testes are situated outside the abdominal cavity within the scrotum primarily because:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Anatomical location of testes
The testes in adult human males are housed outside the abdominal cavity within a pouch of skin termed the scrotum.

Step 2: Thermal requirement of spermatogenesis
Spermatogenesis cannot proceed efficiently at core body temperature (approx. 37°C). The scrotum acts as a thermoregulator, maintaining the testes at 2 to 2.5°C lower than the internal body temperature.

Step 3: Conceptual conclusion
Maintaining this cooler environment of 2 to 2.5°C below core body temperature is strictly necessary for the maturation and production of viable spermatozoa.

answer.text: It maintains a temperature 2 to 2.5°C lower than normal body temperature necessary for spermatogenesis
It maintains a temperature 2 to 2.5°C higher than normal body temperature to facilitate androgen secretion
It protects the testes from high mechanical pressures generated in the thoracic cavity
It provides a higher glycogen reserve essential for Sertoli cell survival

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_HUMANREPRODUCTION_MCQ_Q02 - Compartments inside each adult human testis

questiontext.text: Each adult human testis is divided into approximately how many compartments known as testicular lobules?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Structure of the testis
Each human testis is covered externally by a dense connective tissue capsule called tunica albuginea.

Step 2: Number of lobules
Inward septa divide the interior of each testis into approximately 250 compartments termed testicular lobules.

Step 3: Conceptual conclusion
Thus, each adult human testis contains about 250 testicular lobules, each accommodating one to three highly coiled seminiferous tubules.

answer.text: About 50 compartments
About 250 compartments
About 100 compartments
About 500 compartments

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_HUMANREPRODUCTION_MCQ_Q03 - Sequential pathway of male accessory ducts

questiontext.text: Which of the following represents the correct sequential pathway for the transport of sperms through the male sex accessory ducts?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Identification of starting point
Sperms are initially generated within the highly coiled seminiferous tubules of the testicular lobules.

Step 2: Sequential passage through duct system
The seminiferous tubules open into the vasa efferentia through a network of tubules called the rete testis. The vasa efferentia then exit the testis to empty into the epididymis located along the posterior surface. The epididymis continues as the vas deferens, which ascends into the pelvic cavity.

Step 3: Conceptual conclusion
The accurate anatomical sequence is Seminiferous tubules → Rete testis → Vasa efferentia → Epididymis → Vas deferens.

answer.text: Seminiferous tubules → Vasa efferentia → Rete testis → Vas deferens → Epididymis
Seminiferous tubules → Epididymis → Rete testis → Vasa efferentia → Vas deferens
Seminiferous tubules → Rete testis → Vasa efferentia → Epididymis → Vas deferens
Seminiferous tubules → Rete testis → Epididymis → Vasa efferentia → Vas deferens

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_HUMANREPRODUCTION_MCQ_Q04 - Endocrine role of Leydig interstitial cells

questiontext.text: Which cells located in the interstitial spaces outside the seminiferous tubules synthesize and secrete testicular hormones called androgens?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Histology of seminiferous tubules
The seminiferous tubules are lined internally by spermatogenic germ cells and supportive Sertoli cells.

Step 2: Composition of interstitial space
The regions situated outside the seminiferous tubules are called interstitial spaces, which contain small blood vessels, immunologically competent cells, and interstitial cells (Leydig cells).

Step 3: Conceptual conclusion
Leydig cells are specifically responsible for the synthesis and secretion of male steroid hormones known as androgens, primarily testosterone.

answer.text: Sertoli cells
Spermatogonia
Primary spermatocytes
Leydig cells

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_HUMANREPRODUCTION_MCQ_Q05 - Nutritive function of testicular Sertoli cells

questiontext.text: Inside the seminiferous tubules, what is the primary physiological function of Sertoli cells?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Cell types inside seminiferous tubules
Each seminiferous tubule is lined by two morphologically and functionally distinct cell populations: male germ cells (spermatogonia) and Sertoli cells.

Step 2: Functional role of Sertoli cells
While male germ cells undergo meiotic division to form mature spermatozoa, Sertoli cells act as sustentacular cells that nurse and provide essential nutrients to the differentiating germ cells.

Step 3: Conceptual conclusion
The chief role of Sertoli cells is providing nutrition to developing germ cells and mediating spermiogenesis.

answer.text: Providing nutrition to the developing germ cells
Synthesizing gonadotropin-releasing hormone
Undergoing meiotic division to produce haploid spermatids
Secreting androgens directly into the interstitial spaces

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_HUMANREPRODUCTION_MCQ_Q06 - Composition of male accessory reproductive glands

questiontext.text: Regarding the male accessory glands and their secretions, which of the following statements is biologically accurate?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Cataloguing male accessory glands
The male accessory sex glands consist of paired seminal vesicles, an unpaired (single) prostate gland, and paired bulbourethral (Cowper's) glands.

Step 2: Biochemical nature of seminal plasma
The combined secretions of these accessory glands constitute seminal plasma, which is characteristically rich in fructose, calcium ions, and specific hydrolytic enzymes.

Step 3: Conceptual conclusion
The correct arrangement is paired seminal vesicles, a single prostate gland, and paired bulbourethral glands producing seminal plasma rich in fructose, calcium, and enzymes.

answer.text: The accessory glands comprise a single seminal vesicle, paired prostate glands, and paired bulbourethral glands whose secretions are rich in glucose and bicarbonate
The accessory glands comprise paired seminal vesicles, a single prostate gland, and paired bulbourethral glands whose secretions are rich in fructose, calcium, and specific enzymes
The secretions of the prostate gland alone constitute the entire seminal plasma and lack enzymes or calcium
Seminal vesicles and bulbourethral glands are unpaired structures, whereas the prostate gland is a paired structure

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_HUMANREPRODUCTION_MCQ_Q07 - Lubricating role of bulbourethral gland secretions

questiontext.text: In human males, the mucus secretions of which accessory gland play a significant role in the lubrication of the penis during coitus?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Identification of bulbourethral glands
The bulbourethral glands (also known as Cowper's glands) are paired glands situated on either side of the membranous urethra.

Step 2: Secretory function
Prior to ejaculation, these glands secrete an alkaline, clear, mucoid fluid into the urethra.

Step 3: Conceptual conclusion
This secretion helps neutralize residual acidity in the urethra and provides lubrication to the glans penis to facilitate coitus.

answer.text: Seminal vesicles
Prostate gland
Bulbourethral glands
Epididymis

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_HUMANREPRODUCTION_MCQ_Q08 - Anatomical course of the vas deferens

questiontext.text: Which of the following accurately describes the anatomical path and connection of the vas deferens in the male reproductive tract?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Origin and ascent
The vas deferens arises from the tail of the epididymis, travels upward through the spermatic cord into the abdominal/pelvic cavity.

Step 2: Looping and duct joining
In the pelvis, it curves over the ureter and loops over the urinary bladder. Behind the bladder, it joins the duct of the seminal vesicle.

Step 3: Formation of ejaculatory duct
The union of the vas deferens and seminal vesicle duct forms the short ejaculatory duct, which enters the prostate to open into the urethra.

answer.text: It descends directly from the testis into the scrotum and opens independently into the bulbourethral duct
It ascends into the pelvic cavity, pierces the kidney parenchyma, and opens directly into the ureter
It loops around the rectum, receives ducts from the prostate gland, and terminates blindly in the inguinal canal
It ascends from the epididymis into the abdomen, loops over the urinary bladder, and unites with the duct from the seminal vesicle to form the ejaculatory duct

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_HUMANREPRODUCTION_MCQ_Q09 - Components of the testicular interstitial compartment

questiontext.text: Examination of the interstitial spaces located outside the seminiferous tubules of an adult testis reveals the presence of:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Intratubular vs extratubular compartments
A seminiferous tubule contains spermatogenic cells and Sertoli cells strictly within its internal basement membrane.

Step 2: Extratubular / interstitial tissue
The spaces surrounding the tubules are called interstitial spaces. They contain interstitial connective tissue, small blood vessels, androgen-secreting Leydig cells, and resident immunologically competent cells.

Step 3: Conceptual conclusion
The interstitial spaces specifically house Leydig cells, small blood vessels, and immunologically competent cells.

answer.text: Small blood vessels, Leydig cells, and immunologically competent cells
Spermatogonia, primary spermatocytes, and mature spermatozoa
Sertoli cells, nurse cells, and mature Graafian follicles
Ciliated columnar epithelial cells, podocytes, and myoepithelial cells

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_HUMANREPRODUCTION_MCQ_Q10 - Dimensions and attachments of human ovaries

questiontext.text: In the human female reproductive system, each ovary is about 2 to 4 cm in length and is connected to the pelvic wall and uterus by:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Ovarian anatomy
Ovaries are the primary female sex organs situated on either side of the lower abdomen.

Step 2: Dimensions and ligaments
Each ovary measures about 2 to 4 cm in length and is held in position by peritoneal folds known as ovarian ligaments connected to the pelvic wall and uterus.

Step 3: Conceptual conclusion
Ligaments anchor each ovary securely to both the pelvic wall and the uterine body.

answer.text: Tendons
Ligaments
Muscular sphincters
Cartilaginous bridges

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_HUMANREPRODUCTION_MCQ_Q11 - Sequential regions of the fallopian tube

questiontext.text: What is the correct anatomical order of the regions of the fallopian tube (oviduct) proceeding from the periphery of the ovary towards the uterus?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Oviduct dimensions and structure
Each fallopian tube is 10 to 12 cm long and connects the ovarian vicinity to the uterus.

Step 2: Regional breakdown
The funnel-shaped segment closest to the ovary is the infundibulum, flanked by finger-like fimbriae. The infundibulum opens into the wider ampulla, which leads to the narrow-lumened isthmus joining the uterine cavity.

Step 3: Conceptual conclusion
Moving from ovary to uterus, the order is Fimbriae → Infundibulum → Ampulla → Isthmus.

answer.text: Isthmus → Ampulla → Infundibulum → Fimbriae
Infundibulum → Isthmus → Ampulla → Fimbriae
Fimbriae → Infundibulum → Ampulla → Isthmus
Ampulla → Infundibulum → Isthmus → Fimbriae

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_HUMANREPRODUCTION_MCQ_Q12 - Physiological function of oviductal fimbriae

questiontext.text: What is the primary function of the finger-like projections called fimbriae present at the edges of the infundibulum?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Anatomy of the infundibulum
The infundibulum is the expanded, funnel-shaped terminal end of the oviduct adjacent to the ovary.

Step 2: Role of fimbriae
Its margins bear delicate, ciliated, finger-like extensions termed fimbriae that drape over the ovary.

Step 3: Conceptual conclusion
During ovulation, the rhythmic sweeping motions of the fimbriae draw the released secondary oocyte into the oviductal lumen.

answer.text: Secretion of human chorionic gonadotropin

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_HUMANREPRODUCTION_MCQ_Q13 - Structural layers of the human uterine wall

questiontext.text: Which layer of the uterine wall consists of a thick layer of smooth muscle and exhibits powerful contractions during the delivery of the baby?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Three uterine layers
The wall of the uterus is composed of three distinct tissue layers: an outer thin serous perimetrium, a middle muscular myometrium, and an inner glandular endometrium.

Step 2: Functional specialization
The endometrium lines the cavity and undergoes cyclical sloughing and proliferation during each menstrual cycle. The thick smooth muscle coats of the myometrium contract vigorously under oxytocin stimulation during parturition.

Step 3: Conceptual conclusion
The middle smooth-muscle layer exhibiting powerful labor contractions is the myometrium.

answer.text: Myometrium
Perimetrium
Endometrium
Epimetrium

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_HUMANREPRODUCTION_MCQ_Q14 - Anatomical constituents of the birth canal

questiontext.text: In human reproductive anatomy, the 'birth canal' through which the infant is delivered during parturition is formed jointly by:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Structure of the cervix
The lower, narrow portion of the uterus is the cervix, which communicates with the uterine body above and the vagina below.

Step 2: Formation of the birth canal
The cavity within the cervix is known as the cervical canal. Together with the fibromuscular vaginal canal, it constitutes the passage for child delivery.

Step 3: Conceptual conclusion
The birth canal is explicitly defined as the cervical canal together with the vagina.

answer.text: The uterine cavity and the fallopian tube
The cervical canal and the vagina

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_HUMANREPRODUCTION_MCQ_Q15 - Anatomical position of the human clitoris

questiontext.text: In the human female external genitalia, the clitoris is located at:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: External female genitalia components
The vulva includes the mons pubis, labia majora, labia minora, hymen, and clitoris.

Step 2: Clitoral anatomy
The clitoris is a tiny, highly sensitive, erectile, finger-like organ.

Step 3: Conceptual conclusion
It is situated at the anterior (upper) junction of the two labia minora, positioned superior to the external urethral orifice.

answer.text: The lower junction of the labia majora, below the vaginal orifice

Within the cervical canal, protruding into the upper vagina

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_HUMANREPRODUCTION_MCQ_Q16 - Ductal pathway of milk in mammary gland

questiontext.text: Which of the following represents the correct sequential pathway of milk transport through the mammary gland structures towards the nipple?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Milk synthesis site
Milk is synthesized and secreted by the secretory epithelial cells of the alveoli, clustered inside 15 to 20 mammary lobes.

Step 2: Duct progression
The alveoli open into fine mammary tubules. The tubules of each lobe coalesce to form a mammary duct. Several mammary ducts unite to form a broader reservoir termed the mammary ampulla, which connects to the lactiferous duct exiting at the nipple.

Step 3: Conceptual conclusion
The accurate sequential path is Alveoli → Mammary tubules → Mammary ducts → Mammary ampulla → Lactiferous duct.

answer.text: Alveoli → Mammary ampulla → Mammary ducts → Mammary tubules → Lactiferous duct
Mammary lobes → Lactiferous duct → Mammary ampulla → Alveoli → Mammary tubules
Alveoli → Lactiferous duct → Mammary ducts → Mammary ampulla → Mammary tubules
Alveoli → Mammary tubules → Mammary ducts → Mammary ampulla → Lactiferous duct

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_HUMANREPRODUCTION_MCQ_Q17 - Number of mammary lobes per breast

questiontext.text: The glandular tissue of each human female breast is divided into how many mammary lobes?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Glandular tissue organization
The human female breast consists of variable amounts of adipose tissue and organized glandular tissue.

Step 2: Lobular division
The glandular parenchyma in each breast is partitioned into 15 to 20 distinct mammary lobes containing clusters of milk-secreting alveoli.

Step 3: Conceptual conclusion
Each breast contains 15 to 20 mammary lobes.

answer.text: 15 to 20 lobes
2 to 5 lobes
